text:
Assertion (A): A point P is 13 cm from the centre O of a circle of radius 5 cm. The length of a tangent from P to the circle is 12 cm.
Reason (R): The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

text: Tangents PA and PB are drawn from an external point P to a circle with centre O, touching it at A and B. If ∠APB = 72°, find ∠OAB.
Two concentric circles have radii 10 cm and 6 cm. A chord AB of the larger circle touches the smaller circle at P. Find the length of AB.
A circle has centre O and diameter AB. Tangents are drawn at A and at B. Prove that these two tangents are parallel to each other.
O is the centre of a circle of radius 6 cm and Q is a point 10 cm from O. A student claims that a line QT touches the circle at T and that QT = 9 cm. Is the claim possible? Justify.
A circle is inscribed in ∆ABC and touches sides BC, CA and AB at D, E and F respectively. If AB = 10 cm, BC = 12 cm and CA = 14 cm, find AF, BD and CE.
Tangents PA and PB are drawn from an external point P to a circle with centre O, touching it at A and B. Prove that ∠APB = 2∠OAB.
A circle is inscribed in ∆ABC and touches BC, CA, AB at D, E, F. Prove that BD = (AB + BC − CA) ÷ 2.
A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle, touching AB, BC, CD and DA at P, Q, R and S. Prove that AB + CD = AD + BC.
Two concentric circles have centre O. A chord AB of the larger circle touches the smaller circle at P. Prove that P is the midpoint of AB. Hence, if the radii are 17 cm and 8 cm, find AB.
Tangents PA and PB are drawn from a point P, 25 cm from the centre O, to a circle of radius 7 cm, touching it at A and B. Find the length of the chord AB.
Tangents PA and PB are drawn from an external point P to a circle with centre O. If ∠PAB = (2x + 10)° and ∠PBA = (3x − 20)°, find x and ∠AOB.
A circle has centre O and radius 10 cm. PT is the tangent at T with PT = 24 cm. Find OP and the area of ∆OTP.
In ∆ABC, AB = AC = 13 cm and BC = 10 cm. The incircle touches AB at P, AC at Q and BC at D. Find AP, and show that D is the midpoint of BC.
In ∆ABC, ∠B = 90°, AB = 20 cm and BC = 21 cm, so AC = 29 cm. A circle with centre O touches AB, BC and CA at P, Q and R. Find the radius of the circle and the length AR.
A circle with centre O and radius 4 cm is inscribed in ∆ABC and touches BC at D. BD = 8 cm and DC = 6 cm. The area of ∆ABC is 84 cm². Find the lengths of AB and AC.

Prove that the lengths of the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal. Using this result, prove that if a circle touches all four sides of a parallelogram PQRS, then PQRS is a rhombus.

A circular park has centre O and radius 15 m. A straight road touches the boundary of the park at T. A lamp post P stands on the road, 20 m from T. A second straight road from P also touches the park, at S.
(i) What is the measure of the angle between the radius OT and the road? [1]
(ii) Find the distance OP of the lamp post from the centre of the park. [1]
(iii) Find the length of the chord TS joining the two points of contact. [2]
OR
(iii) Find the area of quadrilateral OTPS. [2]
